LAREDO, Texas — The Prodigy is getting the biggest match of her career — and the whole of Laredo will be watching. Laredo native Roxanne Perez, 24, will challenge Chelsea Green for the WWE Women’s Championship on Friday night’s edition of SmackDown, televised at 7 p.m. on USA Network, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Perez earned the title shot by pinning Green in a non-title match on Oct. 12 at the Brookshire Grocery Arena in Bossier City, Louisiana. Per the Laredo Morning Times, SmackDown General Manager Adam Pearce made the championship match official after the cross-brand situation was settled. It is Perez’s first career televised opportunity at a WWE world championship; her only previous world-title match was a non-televised house-show bout against Stephanie Vaquer in Melbourne, Australia, in October 2025.

From the Laredo Wrestling Alliance to the main roster

Perez’s road to the title picture began in her hometown. According to the Laredo Morning Times, she started wrestling at age 13 with the Laredo Wrestling Alliance, and her rise since has been record-setting: ESPN’s 2024 Women’s Wrestler of the Year, the youngest NXT Champion ever at 21, the youngest two-time NXT champion at 22, and the holder of the longest-duration record in the 2025 Royal Rumble at 67 minutes and 47 seconds. She also competed in this year’s Money in the Bank ladder match, where Tiffany Stratton captured the briefcase for the second straight year.

What a win could mean

The stakes extend beyond Friday night. Perez is a Raw Superstar whose Judgment Day stablemate Liv Morgan already holds Raw’s Women’s World Championship, so a Perez victory could set up a teammates’ showdown at Crown Jewel on Nov. 7, where champions from each brand are set to face off. Wrestling outlets confirmed the title match is officially on the card for the Oct. 23 SmackDown from the Toyota Arena in Ontario, California.
